summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow in gap-closure mode for Phase 68 (ROT-07) of cipher-box, then execute the resulting plans via the execute-phase workflow.
summary.outcome: Planner produced two gap-closure plans (68-11 blocker, 68-12) closing the 2 real gaps from 68-VERIFICATION.md, committed as 566f20455, and plan-checker passed with 0 blockers/warnings; execution then began with Wave 1 (68-11) dispatched to a subagent, with Wave 2 (68-12) still pending when the transcript ends.

repo: cipher-box GSD gap-closure mode reads VERIFICATION.md as the gap source, skips research entirely, and instructs the planner to append new plan numbers (e.g. 68-11+) rather than overwrite existing plans 68-01..68-10
Plans that touch the same shared file across waves (e.g. packages/sdk/src/client.ts) are serialized via depends_on so the wave scheduler never runs them in parallel
SC#5 doctrine: apps/web must stay test-free (no *.spec.ts in apps/web/src); UI/durability behavior is proven via Playwright web-e2e instead
The plan:post gap-analysis hook is advisory/non-blocking and requires the correct subcommand form to invoke (first invocation attempt used wrong form)

code.finding: ensureFolderLoaded is a dead phase-63 stub that throws 'not implemented — phase 63' — it is NOT a live code path despite VERIFICATION.md naming it as the gap-1 target

reconcileFolderSequence is the actual live pre-mutation resolve chokepoint, invoked before every rename/delete/deleteToBin/move (call sites at lines 742, 823-824, 985, 1765) — this is where the fail-closed enforceResolved gate needed to be wired instead of ensureFolderLoaded

performScopeExitRotation is the sole production caller of rotateReadFromNode, which discards the root's rotated {readKey, generation, sequenceNumber} behind a void return — changing the return type to RotateReadResult|undefined is backward compatible

workflow: GSD orchestrators must wait for a spawned subagent (planner/checker/executor) to return rather than touching the same files it's editing, per orchestrator protocol
task-notification can fire more than once for the same task-id since the agent can be resumed — don't assume first notification is final without checking

When config has conflicting auto_advance:true and mode:interactive and the plans touch security-sensitive fail-closed crypto code, GSD should stop and confirm via AskUserQuestion rather than silently auto-advancing
GSD's commit-helper can report commit_failed as a false negative when the commit actually landed — verify via git log/git status rather than retrying the commit

friction: Config conflict between auto_advance:true and mode:interactive required pausing for an explicit user decision before launching execution on security-sensitive crypto code
Regenerated API-SURFACE.md hint came back with 0 symbols (uninformative) and had to be omitted from the planner's read list
First attempt at the post-planning gap-analysis check used the wrong subcommand and had to be re-run with the correct one
GSD commit-helper reported a false-negative commit_failed status requiring manual git log/status verification to confirm the commit actually landed
